questions.question: What does the Stop traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Stop before proceeding when this sign controls the approach.

questions.question: What does the Give Way traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Give way to traffic as required at the controlled junction.

questions.question: What does the No Entry traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Entry is prohibited in the direction controlled by the sign.

questions.question: What does the No Motor Vehicles traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Motor vehicles are prohibited beyond the sign where the restriction applies.

questions.question: What does the No Overtaking traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Overtaking is prohibited where the restriction applies.

questions.question: What does the Maximum Speed Limit traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Do not exceed the speed shown on the sign.

questions.question: What does the No Parking traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Parking is prohibited where this restriction applies.

questions.question: What does the No Stopping traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Stopping is prohibited where this restriction applies.

questions.question: What does the Compulsory Keep Left traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Pass to the left of the traffic island or obstruction as indicated.

questions.question: What does the Compulsory Ahead traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Proceed straight ahead in the direction indicated by the sign.

questions.question: What does the Left Hand Curve traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: A left-hand curve is ahead.

questions.question: What does the Right Hand Curve traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: A right-hand curve is ahead.

questions.question: What does the Hairpin Bend traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: A very sharp bend is ahead; slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.question: What does the Narrow Road Ahead traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: The road narrows ahead; reduce speed and be prepared for conflicting traffic.

questions.question: What does the Narrow Bridge Ahead traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: A narrow bridge is ahead; approach with care.

questions.question: What does the Pedestrian Crossing Ahead traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: A pedestrian crossing is ahead; slow down and be prepared to yield as required.

questions.question: What does the School Ahead traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: A school or school-zone activity is ahead; exercise extra caution.

questions.question: What does the Men at Work traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Road works or workmen may be present ahead; slow down and follow temporary controls.

questions.question: What does the Slippery Road traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: The road surface may be slippery; reduce speed and avoid sudden manoeuvres.

questions.question: What does the Speed Breaker traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: A speed breaker/hump is ahead; slow down before crossing it.

questions.question: What does the Parking traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Identifies a parking facility or designated parking location.

questions.question: What does the Hospital traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Indicates a hospital or hospital facility.

questions.question: What does the First Aid Post traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Indicates a first-aid facility.

questions.question: What does the Filling Station traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Indicates a petrol/fuel filling station.

questions.question: What does the Bus Stop traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Identifies a designated bus stop.

questions.question: What does the Taxi Stand traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Identifies a location where taxis may wait when not engaged.

questions.question: What does the Police Station traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Indicates a nearby police station.

questions.question: What does the No Through Road traffic sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Indicates that the road ahead does not provide through passage.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Separates opposing streams of traffic; follow the applicable road marking and traffic rules.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Centre Line. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: A broken centre line generally indicates that crossing may be permitted when safe and otherwise lawful.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Broken Centre Line. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: A solid centre line indicates a restriction on crossing that line; follow the applicable marking and road conditions.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Solid Centre Line. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Double solid lines indicate a stronger restriction against crossing between opposing traffic streams.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Double Solid Centre Line. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Separates lanes travelling in the same direction.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Lane Line. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Marks lane separation where a lane change may be possible when safe and lawful.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Broken Lane Line. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Marks the edge of the carriageway.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Edge Line. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Indicates where a vehicle should stop at a controlled stop point.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Stop Line. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Indicates where a driver should yield according to the applicable give-way control.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Give-Way Line. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Marks a pedestrian crossing area; drivers must approach with appropriate caution and yield as required.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Zebra Crossing. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Provides visual guidance approaching a pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Pedestrian Crossing Approach Marking. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Indicates permitted or intended straight-ahead movement for the lane.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Directional Arrow — Straight. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Indicates permitted or intended left movement for the lane.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Directional Arrow — Left. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Indicates permitted or intended right movement for the lane.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Directional Arrow — Right. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Indicates that the lane is intended for straight or left movement.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Straight-or-Left Arrow. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Indicates that the lane is intended for straight or right movement.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Straight-or-Right Arrow. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Yellow markings may indicate a stopping/parking restriction depending on the applicable road standard and location.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Yellow Edge/Restriction Line. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Marks a location where parking is restricted according to the applicable sign/marking scheme.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is No-Parking Marking. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Marks a location where stopping is restricted according to the applicable sign/marking scheme.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is No-Stopping Marking. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: A marked junction area intended to keep the intersection clear; do not enter unless your exit is clear where the applicable rule requires it.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Box Junction. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Separates or channels traffic and should not normally be entered except where permitted by the applicable road marking.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Hatched Area. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Guides traffic around an obstruction or traffic island; avoid entering the marked area unless permitted.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Chevron/Diagonal Area. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Identifies a designated stopping area for buses where provided.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Bus Stop Marking. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Identifies a lane or space intended for cycles where provided.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Cycle Lane Marking. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: Which road marking is described by: Defines a marked parking space; use remains subject to signs and local restrictions.
questions.explanation: The correct marking is Parking Bay Marking. Treat the visual as educational guidance and follow the applicable current road standard.

questions.question: What should you do before applying for a learner licence?
options: Confirm the intended vehicle class and selected jurisdiction.
Confirm the vehicle class and jurisdiction
Use any State without selecting one.
questions.explanation: The vehicle class and jurisdiction affect the applicable process and requirements.

questions.question: Where should State/UT-specific document requirements be checked?
options: The current official State/UT transport or Sarathi process.
The current official State/UT transport or Sarathi process
questions.explanation: State/UT adaptation can affect the exact document list.

questions.question: Which official form is the physical-fitness self declaration?
questions.explanation: Parivahan's current Form 1 is the application-cum-declaration as to physical fitness.

questions.question: Which form is the medical certificate?
questions.explanation: Form 1A is the medical certificate; applicability depends on the case.

questions.question: What does the preliminary learner test cover?
options: Knowledge such as traffic signs, traffic signals, accident duties and documents.
Traffic signs, signals, accident duties and documents
questions.explanation: The official Form 2 material identifies these knowledge areas.

questions.question: What should you do after a wrong practice answer?
options: Read the explanation and linked knowledge item.
Read the explanation and linked knowledge item
questions.explanation: RTOBuddy's purpose is learning, not just scoring.

questions.question: Why does RTOBuddy label some jurisdiction data as unverified?
options: Because legal-sensitive State/UT details should be confirmed against current official sources.
Because the app cannot display JSON
Because current official verification is still pending
Because all State rules are identical
questions.explanation: Unverified data should not be presented as official legal advice.

questions.question: What is the safest source for current application workflow?
options: The current official Parivahan/Sarathi or State transport portal.
questions.explanation: Portal workflows can change.

questions.question: What should you retain after an online application when issued?
options: Only a screenshot of the home page
questions.explanation: References are useful for status, printing and appointment actions.

questions.question: What should a learner do while practising?
options: Follow learner conditions and road rules
Follow the learner-licence conditions and applicable road rules.
questions.explanation: A learner licence does not remove road-safety obligations.

questions.question: Can every learner be assumed to need Form 1A?
options: No; applicability depends on the case.
No; applicability depends on the case
questions.explanation: The official document list marks Form 1A as applicable in specified cases.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a document checklist?
options: To prepare the likely required documents before starting the official process.
To prepare documents before the official process
questions.explanation: The checklist is a preparation aid, not a substitute for the official process.

questions.question: What should you do if RTOBuddy and the official portal disagree?
options: Prefer the current official source and flag the RTOBuddy content for review.
Always trust the older app data
questions.explanation: RTOBuddy is an educational layer and must yield to current official information.

questions.question: What does 'jurisdiction overlay' mean in RTOBuddy?
options: State/UT-specific information layered over the national baseline
State/UT-specific information layered over the national baseline.
questions.explanation: This is the core data architecture.

questions.question: Why are fees kept out of the national baseline?
options: They can vary by jurisdiction and change over time
They can vary by jurisdiction and change over time.
questions.explanation: Dynamic/legal-sensitive values should be versioned and jurisdiction-specific.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the learner-test practice bank?
options: To rehearse test knowledge and explanations
To rehearse the knowledge areas likely to be tested and learn from explanations.
questions.explanation: Practice supports preparation; it does not issue a licence.

questions.question: What should you check before a permanent driving test?
options: That the learner licence is valid and covers the intended class, plus the current official procedure.
Licence validity/class and current official procedure
questions.explanation: The official permanent-licence procedure requires a valid learner licence for the relevant class.

questions.question: Why does RTOBuddy show source IDs?
options: To make the provenance of legal-sensitive content traceable.
questions.explanation: Source metadata makes review and updating easier.

questions.question: What does 'source_verified' mean in RTOBuddy?
options: It is guaranteed by the app forever
It was checked against the cited source at the recorded verification date
The content was checked against the cited source at the recorded verification date.
questions.explanation: Verification is time-bound; current law can change.

questions.question: What is the recommended approach for a new learner?
options: Learn, practise, review weak areas, then use the official process.
Learn, practise, review weak areas, then use the official process
questions.explanation: The app is designed as a learning companion.

questions.question: At a steady Red traffic signal, what should a driver do?
options: Stop before the stop line and wait until green
Speed up to clear the junction quickly
Slow down only if other vehicles are present
questions.explanation: A steady red means stop and remain stopped until the signal permits you to proceed.

questions.question: At a steady Amber / Yellow traffic signal, what is the correct action?
options: Stop if you can do so safely; do not race the light
Treat it the same as a green signal
Park inside the junction until green
questions.explanation: Amber warns that red is coming. Stop if you can do so safely; proceed only if stopping would be unsafe.

questions.question: At a steady Green traffic signal, what should a driver do?
options: Proceed if the way is clear and it is otherwise lawful
Stop and wait as if the light were red
Ignore pedestrians already on the crossing
Enter the junction even when it is blocked
questions.explanation: Green permits movement only when the path is clear and other rules (like giving way) are still followed.

questions.question: What should a driver do at a Flashing Red traffic signal?
options: Stop completely, then proceed only when safe
Continue at normal speed without stopping
Treat it the same as a steady green
questions.explanation: Flashing red works like a stop control: stop, check, then go only when safe.

questions.question: What should a driver do at a Flashing Amber / Yellow traffic signal?
options: Slow down, check carefully, and proceed with caution
Stop permanently until an officer waves you on
Treat it the same as a steady red
Speed up because flashing means free passage
questions.explanation: Flashing amber means caution: reduce speed, look for cross traffic or pedestrians, then proceed carefully.

questions.question: When an ambulance with flashing lights and siren approaches from behind, what must you do?
options: Speed up to get out of its way
Pull over to the left and let it pass
Stop in the middle of the road
Ignore it if you have right of way
questions.explanation: Under MVA section 194(E), all vehicles must give way to emergency vehicles (ambulance, fire) with active lights/siren by moving to the left side of the road.
